land.text: 'The Kingdom of Janggala comprised the northeastern part of the Kingdom of Kahuripan'
the whole kingdom: Kameswara of Kadiri 'married a princess of the Kingdom of Janggala' in 1136 'at which point the Kingdom of Janggala ceased to exist'

successors.note: Cliopatria's Kediri shape grows to Janggala's size in 1139; the same page also credits Jayabaya with taking Janggala in 1135-1157, and Legge (quoted there) with the reunion under Ken Angrok.

capitals.name: Hujung Galuh (Surabaya)
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Capital: Hujung Galuh (Surabaya)', 'located on the estuarine of Brantas river'. The page dates no move.

correction.text: the shape unchanged, but holding from 1045: the kingdom was 'formed when Airlangga abdicated his throne in favour of his two sons in 1045', and 'comprised the northeastern part of the Kingdom of Kahuripan'

keyframe_review.note: Years only: Cliopatria begins in 1046, the page in 1045. 34,429 km2: on the grid 127 of East Java's 197 cells and 8 of Central Java's, i.e. the eastern part of Kahuripan, matching 'northeastern part'. The page gives no area to compare.

correction.text: the shape unchanged but ending in 1136, not 1138: Kameswara 'married a princess of the Kingdom of Janggala' in 1136, 'at which point the Kingdom of Janggala ceased to exist'

keyframe_review.note: Years only: the infobox says 'uniting the two: 1136'; Cliopatria's Janggala runs to 1138 and the enlarged Kediri shape starts in 1139. The same page also says 'Kadiri took over the eastern Janggala empire under the command of Jayabaya in 1135-1157', so the end is a union of the crowns in 1136 rather than a dated conquest.

region.text: 'the northeastern part of the Kingdom of Kahuripan'

ledger.note: 1045: Janggala is formed in the partition of Kahuripan. The page: 'formed when Airlangga abdicated his throne in favour of his two sons in 1045'; infobox 'Airlangga divided his kingdom into Janggala and Panjalu (Kediri): 1045'. Its ruler list starts earlier ('1042 - 1052: Mapanji Garasakan'), and the Kediri Kingdom article (see the kediri-kingdom dossier) dates the division to 1042.

region.text: the frontier between Kediri (Panjalu) and Janggala; the page names no ground

ledger.note: 1049: civil war between Janggala and Panjalu after Airlangga's death. Kahuripan page: 'Airlanga died in 1049' and 'After the death of Airlangga, a civil war broke out between Janggala and Panjalu that continued until 1052.' The page names no campaign or ground; the Janggala page describes no such war.

region.text: the frontier between Kediri (Panjalu) and Janggala; the page names no ground

ledger.note: 1052: the civil war with Panjalu ends. 'a civil war broke out between Janggala and Panjalu that continued until 1052.' Neither page says who won or that a border moved; both kingdoms continue with the same Cliopatria shapes.

1135: Kediri moves on Janggala under Jayabaya. 'A century later Kadiri took over the eastern Janggala empire under the command of Jayabaya in 1135-1157.' The dates are Jayabaya's reign (the Kediri Kingdom article: 'Jayabhaya (1135-1159)'), not campaign dates; the same page ends Janggala by marriage in 1136.
1136: the fighting ends in a union of the crowns. Infobox: 'Kameswara of Kadiri married a princess of the Kingdom of Janggala, uniting the two: 1136'.

1136: Janggala passes to Kediri. 'Kameswara (1116-1136) married a princess of the Kingdom of Janggala... at which point the Kingdom of Janggala ceased to exist.' Cliopatria draws the enlarged Kediri from 1139.

1136: Janggala ends. The page: 'The Kingdom of Janggala ceased to exist' on the union with Kediri; it also quotes Legge, 'The successor kingdoms of Kadiri and Djanggala were in due course reunited under Ken Angrok', which contradicts the 1136 union.

wars.name: Janggala-Panjalu civil war

zones.text: the frontier between Kediri (Panjalu) and Janggala; the page names no ground

wars.outcome: Fighting between the two halves of Kahuripan after Airlangga's death; the page gives no victor and no change of frontier.
wars.note: Only the Kahuripan page dates it; the Janggala page describes no war between the two before Jayabaya.

wars.name: Kediri's absorption of Janggala under Jayabaya
wars.outcome: Janggala is taken over by Kediri; the page ends it with the 1136 marriage of Kameswara to a Janggala princess.
wars.note: 'A century later Kadiri took over the eastern Janggala empire under the command of Jayabaya in 1135-1157.' The page's dates conflict: Kameswara 1116-1136 versus Jayabaya 1135-1157.

certainty.note: The only boundary on the page is the legend of a river made by Mpu Bharada's water; the line between Janggala and Kediri is Cliopatria's.

sources.title: Janggala
sources.note: Identity, 1045 formation, capital, territory ('northeastern part of the Kingdom of Kahuripan'), 1136 union with Kediri. No area in the infobox.

sources.title: Kahuripan
sources.note: The partition of 1045, Airlangga's death in 1049 and the civil war to 1052.

notes: Page budget 1-2 pages: Janggala and Kahuripan. Disagreements: the Janggala page gives both a 1136 union by marriage and Jayabaya's conquest 1135-1157, and quotes Legge for a reunion under Ken Angrok (1222); the ruler list starts in 1042, the partition in 1045; the Kediri Kingdom article says 1042. Cliopatria's end year 1138 is two years later than the page's 1136. The Janggala page names no neighbour, boundary or vassal besides Kediri. The 1049-1052 war is on the Kahuripan page only. Cliopatria neighbours: early-balinese-kingdoms 1046-1138 (no event: Bali lay outside both successors). No new gazetteer names needed.
